correctness.rationale: For all a,b,c>=0, literal palindromic cyclic factors of length <=n=a+b+c+3 partition disjointly by number of ones 0,1,2,3. Exhaustive string templates yield the three-case closed formula, including zero and equal gaps. Distinct-gap optimization forces largest gap c>=ceil(n/3), with all equality triples solved exactly; n>=14 makes the repeated-gap count strictly lower by floor(n/2)-ceil(n/3)-1>=1. Standalone finite checks of 7140 ordered configurations for n<=36 and brute extremizers n=14..24 passed; universal proof does not rely on finite checks.

evidence: Simpson (2014) Theorem 7: the maximum for all length-n circular words is strictly less than 5n/3. Lemma 6 gives only a lower construction for n divisible by three. Open question (2) discusses optimality of proposed families.

originality.rationale: Simpson (2014) obtains unrestricted upper bound <5n/3, provides three-marker lower constructions for multiples of three and proposes extremal families but does not classify all three-marker words or their exact maximizers. The stronger gap-dependent formula and complete dihedral equality classification for every n>=14 do not follow from Simpson's upper/lower bounds, numerical OEIS table, or the distinct periodicity-equation results of Blondin Massé et al. (2011). Search and inspected literature did not show dominating results; unindexed overlap remains a risk.

value.rationale: The original 2014 circular-palindrome extremal program singles out three-marker Biggles words as near-extremizers. This gives a natural complete all-length classification of precisely that candidate family, proves exact optimality within the family and uniqueness/two-type dihedral extremizers, and explains the rigid equal-gap count versus maximum-gap behavior. It provides an analytic obstruction to every alternative sparse three-marker extremizer, not merely finite numerical increments. The boundary to the open unrestricted problem is explicit.
